key_insight: DMuon makes Muon practical for distributed training by cutting optimizer overhead to near-AdamW levels without changing the training framework.
engineering_relevance: It provides a drop-in path to use matrix-orthogonalization optimizers at scale in both embodied foundation models and large language model training.
method: Integrates as a drop-in module with no framework-level changes
Uses efficient handling of matrix-level updates and Newton-Schulz iterations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 1.48x-3.01x end-to-end step-time speedup and 6.85x-163.00x optimizer-step speedup across embodied foundation model and LLM workloads.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on the cost of matrix-shaped updates and distributed communication patterns, so results may vary by architecture and training stack.
paper_title: DMuon: Efficient Distributed Muon Training with Near-Adam Overhead
